findings.description: SHEET-MARK-001 says the settle pass polls 'with a bounded timeout' — wording that reads as a wall-clock deadline. All three A-direction sketches independently invented exactly that: a `SettleConfig`/config struct carrying `poll_interval: Duration` + `timeout: Duration`, with `Instant::now()`/`.elapsed()` used to decide when the bound is hit (A1's `start.elapsed() >= cfg.timeout`, A2's `Instant::now() + timeout` deadline, A3's identical `Instant::now() + cfg.timeout`). This is spec-traced (it follows directly from the word 'timeout') and is genuinely absent from the real implementation: `crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs`'s actual `SettleConfig` has a single field, `pub max_polls: u32` (default 8) — no `Duration`, no `Instant`, no wall-clock arithmetic anywhere in `read_marks`'s loop, which simply increments a `polls` counter and breaks at `polls >= cfg.max_polls`. All three B-direction reconstructions correctly recovered this actual mechanism (B1/B2/B3 all state 'up to `SettleConfig.max_polls` (default 8)' as the bound, a fixed retry-COUNT, not a timer). A real-world consequence: under `max_polls`, a slow network adding latency per poll consumes the SAME fixed budget as a fast one — the opposite of what a literal 'timeout' (a time budget, poll count unconstrained) would do. Both directions independently surface this same underlying spec/code mismatch: the spec's bound is time-shaped, the code's bound is count-shaped.

The Transient/Permanent classification boundary is pinned by exact string rules SHEET-MARK-001's 'terminally errored' phrase never states, and all three B outputs agree on it verbatim: empty, case-insensitive 'Loading...', or the EXACT string "#N/A" -> Transient (keep polling); any OTHER text starting with '#' (e.g. "#ERROR!", "#REF!") -> Permanent immediately; text that parses as f64 -> Numeric; any other non-#, non-parsing text -> ALSO Permanent (`price_reading_from_cells` in `crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs`). Notably, 2 of 3 A-direction sketches (A1, A2) guessed differently — both treat ANY #-prefixed string, including bare "#N/A", as terminal on first sighting, with no transient carve-out. Only A3 flagged this exact line as 'the most ambiguous call in the EARS' and split it the way the real code does. The spec text supports neither reading over the other — it's silent on the distinction entirely.

A whole secondary degrade/carry-forward protocol is code- and test-enforced with zero counterpart in the given spec text or in any A-direction sketch: three named `DegradeReason`s (`TimedOut`, `Permanent`, `SubCent`); a converted price rounding to <=0 cents degrades `SubCent` (never a zero/negative mark, `price_to_cents`); a non-finite price degrades `Permanent`; a symbol still Transient/absent after the whole poll window CARRIES FORWARD its prior cycle's good `Mark` unchanged if one exists (`transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window`), degrading `TimedOut` only when no prior mark exists; a `Permanent` reading settles that symbol's loop immediately without consuming remaining poll budget and NEVER carries a prior mark forward (`permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry`); and degraded symbols are omitted entirely from `MarksProduced::to_ledger_marks()` — never present as 0/null. None of A1/A2/A3 model prior-mark carry-forward or a SubCent/Permanent/TimedOut three-way split with different carry rules; this apparatus is simply invisible from 'polling... until numeric or terminally errored, with a bounded timeout.'

The price->Cents rounding rule is fully pinned in code and tests — `round_half_to_even(price_usd × 100)` computed via a ×1,000,000 integer micro-cent scale (`price_to_cents`), confirmed by an explicit banker's-rounding test (`1.005 -> $1.00`, `1.015 -> $1.02`). SHEET-MARK-001 says nothing about rounding or Cents conversion at all; A1/A2/A3 each punt on this ('Cents conversion assumed downstream' / 'not shown here' / an unspecified `dollars_to_cents` helper), correctly flagging it as unspecified rather than inventing a matching rule.

The offline/cold-start contract is pinned by an explicit test the EARS text doesn't anticipate: if `read_price_pass` itself errors (workbook offline/unreachable), `read_marks` propagates the `Err` and produces NO `MarksProduced` at all — it must NOT silently emit an empty marks set, per `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks`. Separately, a Positions tab that doesn't exist yet reads back as an empty `PricePass` (cold start), not an error (`ViewSheetsAdapter::read_price_pass`). Neither branch (hard-propagate-on-transport-error vs. soft-empty-on-missing-tab) is suggested by 'polling the Price cells... with a bounded timeout,' and no A sketch distinguishes these two failure modes.

Concrete column layout is pinned in code that the spec text is silent on: `Price` is column index 4, the companion `Quote Date` is column index 12, parsed as `i32` and defaulting to `0` if missing/unparseable; the Quote Date itself is a locale-proof 'days since 1970-01-01' integer serial produced by `IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE(...,"tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` rather than any wall-clock read timestamp. SHEET-MARK-001 only says 'the Price cells' — no column indices, no companion quote-date field, no locale-proofing scheme. All three B outputs recovered this identically; no A sketch has any reason to invent it.

notes:
A-direction agreement is medium: all three converge on treating 'bounded timeout' as a wall-clock Duration/Instant deadline, structural (not runtime-enforced) separation from the formula write, and a single shared deadline across all rows/symbols (not per-cell) — but they diverge on shape-level details with no spec basis either way: A1 fails the WHOLE batch with Err(SettleError::Timeout{unresolved}) on timeout, whereas A2/A3 return Ok with a per-symbol soft MarkResult::TimedOut/Mark::TimedOut variant; A1/A3 batch all cells in one read_price_cells call per poll, A2 reads one row at a time; and A1/A2 vs A3 split 2-1 on whether a bare \"#N/A\" gets a transient carve-out. These are invented-interface disagreements (no EARS text basis either way) rather than findings themselves, but they lower A's stability from high to medium.\n\nB-direction agreement is high: B1/B2/B3 agree near-verbatim on every material constant and rule recovered from the code — SettleConfig.max_polls default 8 as a poll-COUNT bound (not a timer), the exact Transient/Permanent string-classification boundary (blank/\"Loading...\"/exact \"#N/A\" -> Transient; other '#' text -> Permanent; parses f64 -> Numeric; else -> Permanent), the round_half_to_even ×1,000,000 rounding rule and its SubCent/Permanent degrade splits, the prior-mark carry-forward-on-timeout vs. no-carry-on-Permanent distinction, the offline-propagates-Err / missing-tab-reads-empty split, and Price=col4/Quote Date=col12 with i32-default-0 parsing. The three differ only in EARS-ID labeling scheme (U/E/S/N groupings) and prose ordering, not in substance.

The single strongest finding (bounded timeout: spec text implies a wall-clock deadline; code implements a fixed poll-COUNT of 8 with no timer at all) is a genuine BD-DRIFT — surfaced independently and convergently by both directions from their respective sole sources. Everything else recovered by the B-direction (the degrade-reason apparatus, carry-forward semantics, rounding rule, offline/cold-start contract, column layout) is pure code-side surplus with no A-side counterpart, since none of it is even hinted at in the one-sentence SHEET-MARK-001 text given.
